newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY GRAINS REVERSE RISING TREND SUDDENLY.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY GRAINS REVERSE RISING TREND SUDDENLY.

text.p: Hungary's grains futures market was unnerved by a U-turn in prices on Wednesday following recent sharp rises on concerns over the crop's quality after excessive rains, traders said.
The market was in the dark over what damage the bad weather had done in the crop, traders said.

Some of them said Wednesday's price falls were caused by profit-takings in a technical correction, while others were confident that fears had been exaggerated and futures would set a pattern of decline for the longer term.
"It is very difficult to decide now who is right," said Dezso Kormendi of LaSalle Rt. "But I think the market will consolidate now and price levels will descend for the longer term."
"Everybody is uncertain," said Antal Szoke of Agrimpex. "One thing is sure, there are serious problems with the crop's quality."

He said the gluten content of the crop was below the 29 percent minimum of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), while Kormendi said the high amount of the wheat crop, 5.5 million should ensure enough quality wheat for the domestic market.
The BCE's grains futures turnover was a light 369 million forints, down from Tuesday's 407 million forints.
Milling wheat futures, freed up after three days of limit-up movement, fell by 250 to 1,000 forints on Wednesday, compared with a 400 forint rise for almost all maturities on Tuesday.
August milling wheat eased 250 forints to 25,790 per tonne, October fell 1,000 forints to 27,000 while the December price was settled at 28,000 forints, down 930.
Maize and feed barley futures followed the milling wheat and reversed a previous rising trend.
Feed wheat futures extended their losses, falling 400 forints for all the maturities traded on Wednesday.
